EBITDA & EBITDA Margin
charts.annotation: EBITDA includes Couche-Tard's share of joint-venture earnings (JVShareOfEarnings) -- see the JV chart below for that component on its own.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

jvEarnings.title: Share of joint-venture earnings
jvEarnings.content:
Share of joint-venture earnings is Couche-Tard's pro-rata share of the net income of businesses it does not wholly own or consolidate (e.g. its CrossAmerica and other fuel-supply/retail joint ventures), recognised below the operating line under the equity method.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: this line is folded into the company's EBITDA figure shown above, so a swing here moves reported EBITDA without any change in the wholly-owned network's own operating performance -- FY2023's drop to $3.8m (from the ~$20-30m run rate either side) depressed that year's EBITDA for reasons outside the core store/fuel business.

What to watch:

  • Size relative to total EBITDA (small in absolute terms, but lumpy year to year)
  • Whether a move here is a one-off at the JV level rather than a core-business trend

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

networkSites.title: Total network sites
networkSites.content:
Total network sites is Couche-Tard's own disclosed count of convenience/fuel sites across its entire global network -- company-operated plus franchised, licensed and other affiliated sites -- not just the company-operated store count tracked elsewhere.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: this is the scale metric a convenience-store rollup is actually judged on; it moves in large steps (acquisitions such as the FY2024 jump) rather than the smooth, continuous curve of organic same-store growth.

What to watch:

  • Site count growth versus revenue growth -- are new sites adding proportionate sales, or is growth all from the existing footprint
  • Acquisition-driven step changes versus organic network growth (including site closures/divestitures)

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
